parts.part_name: Being Smart About What You Share
What To Do When People Ask For Information?

review_lesson.title: Private vs Public Information
review_lesson.message:
Some things are safe to share, and others should be kept private.

Public Information (OK to share):
<ul>Your favorite color<li>Your favorite game or show<li>Your pet's name**

review_lesson.title: Private vs Public Information
review_lesson.message:
Private Information (keep safe):
<ul>Full name<li>Home address<li>Phone number<li>Birthday**

Private information can be used to identify or contact you. Only <v>trustworthy** adults should know it.

review_lesson.title: Why Does this Matter
review_lesson.message: Knowing the difference helps you stay safe online. If you share too much private information—even by accident—someone could use it to figure out who you are or where you live.

review_lesson.title: Why Does this Matter Continued
review_lesson.message:
That's why you should always ask yourself:
<ul>Is this public or private?<li>Who will see it?<li>Should I ask a <v>trustworthy** adult first?**

review_lesson.title: How Small Details Add Up
review_lesson.message:
Even if you don't share your full name or address, small pieces of information can still reveal a lot about you.

For example: Saying 'I just turned 10' tells others your age or mentioning your soccer team and school name tells others where you go to school.

When someone puts all these clues together, they can learn private things about you without you realizing it.

review_lesson.title: Think Before You Share
review_lesson.message:
Before posting or sharing anything online, ask yourself these questions:
<ul>Is this private information?<li>Who can see this?<li>Does this reveal too much?**

If you're ever unsure, always check with a <v>trustworthy** adult before sharing.

options.title: Red Flags to Watch Out For

review_lesson.title: Red Flags to Watch Out For
review_lesson.message:
Not everyone online is who they say they are. Some people pretend to be friendly to try and get your private information.

<b>Watch out for these red flags:**
<ul>They ask for your name, school, address, or birthday.<li>They want to meet you in real life.<li>They ask for pictures or personal details.<li>They tell you to keep your conversation a secret.<li>They offer you gifts or prizes in exchange for information.**

options.title: What to Do If a Strangers Asks For Information Online

review_lesson.title: What to Do If a Strangers Asks For Information Online
review_lesson.message:
If This Happens:
<ul>Don't respond or share anything<li>Tell a <v>trustworthy** adult right away<li>Block and report the person if they keep asking<li>Trust your instincts—if it feels off, it probably is**

review_lesson.title: Golden Rule
review_lesson.message:
Golden Rule:
If a stranger online asks for personal info, STOP and ASK a <v>trustworthy** adult before you do anything.

message.text: I landed on the moon, I must find Alejandro!
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: Hi Alejandro, I'm Cyber Hero. Patrick the Predatoraus just arrived. Allie sent me to help you keep the Privacy Planet's information protected.
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: Huh? How do I know you are telling the truth? Do you really know Allie?
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: Yeah, and she's taught me lessons on <v>sensitive data** and information. Ask me anything if you think I'm lying!
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: Hmmm okay! What is public information?
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
Public information is safe share with anyone. Like:
<ul>Your Favorite Color<li>Your Hobbies<li>A Fun Fact About Yourself**
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: What is private information?
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: Private (or sensitive) information should only be shared with trusted adults because it can be used to identify or contact you.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: Wow! Allie has taught you well! I trust you now. Let's go defeat Patrick and get people's private information back!
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: I don't understand. How did Patrick manage to get everyone's private information? Surely you guys didn't just freely share them.
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: Patrick is smart. He can find out information about you just with little details like pieces of a puzzle.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
<red>Small details add up!!**

Patrick got my information because a few weeks ago, I decorated my Roblox avatar with a birthday hat and typed in the chat: "It's my birthday! I just turned 10!"
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: So now he knows your age!
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: Yup! And then a few weeks later, I made a post about my soccer game and mentioned my school's name in the chat.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: And that's how he learned where you go to school?
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: Yeah! Then I also left a comment on a friend's game saying: "Let's play after school at the park near the red slide." So now Patrick even knows where I hang out.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
Patrick pieced together all these clues and learned about:
<ul>My age<li>My school<li>A place I visit often**
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: Even though you never shared your full name or address, they now still know a lot about you?
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text: Yes! That's why it's important to think before you post.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
<u>Ask yourself:** Is this information private? If it includes your name, location, or contact details:
<red>DON'T SHARE IT!**
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: <u>Then ask yourself:** Who can see this? Some things are public like gamertags, usernames, and profile pictures. This means that anyone can see them - even people you don't know.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: <u>Finally, think:** Does this reveal too much? A fun picture of you in a school t-shirt might seem okay, but if it shows your school's name, it could tell strangers where you go every day.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: If you are still unsure, it is always a good idea to check with a trusted adult.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: Sometimes, people online might ask you for personal details. Do not share even if they seem friendly or nice.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: They could pretend to be another kid or someone you can trust. Here, I'll give you some <v>scenario**s, and you tell me if they're a red flag or green flag.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text: What should I do if someone asks me that?
message.speaker: Cyber Hero

message.text:
<red>Never respond or give out your information.**
Even if the person seems nice or <v>trustworthy**, it's important to stay cautious. Strangers online may not be who they say they are, and sharing even small details can put you at risk.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
<red>Tell a trusted adult right away.**
If someone makes you feel uncomfortable, asks for personal details, or pressures you to share something, report to a parent, teacher, or <v>guardian**. They can help you decide what to do next.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
<red>Block or report the person if they keep asking questions.**
Most websites and apps have <v>feature**s that allow you to block or report users who are acting suspiciously. This helps keeping you and the others safe.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
<red>Trust your instincts.**
If something feels off about a conversation, listen to that feeling. It's always better to be cautious than to take a risk.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
Remember that even if someone seems nice, they might not be who they say they are.
<red>Online, people can pretend to be anyone.**
They might use fake pictures, names, or stories to trick others into trusting them.
message.speaker: Alejandro

message.text:
If a stranger online asks you anything personal -
<red>STOP and ask an adult before responding!**
message.speaker: Alejandro
